utterances.text: I also just want to remind you that at this time you agreed that there were enormous amount of people around this house at the time, that's what you said on Monday, there were a lot of people around?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And you not only that -- you said there was a lot on your mind at this time, you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. Now this person that you say was not the plain soldier, where did you first observe this person. Please mark him.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: It was on the paved road next to the "White House", the first road that I saw, and this road here. And I saw him here halfway, halfway that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: M'hm. All right. Well, perhaps if you can do an actual mark, please, an X, and right the initials PS.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Should be actually NPS, not plain soldier, all right? Can you put N there for me.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Oh, yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Do you have that there? Right. Now, we've established that in the first 15 minutes Major you are moving around a lot, around the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? So the first time that you see this person is that -- that's after you've already been there for 15 minutes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And it is not a case at all, is it, that you at any stage had this person under surveillance for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You weren't observing them for the whole time were you?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: At best, it would be a fleeting observation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No. We were sometime at the opposite of the "White House", in front of the gate. There was the situation that I spoke about with some colleagues at the opposite of the "White House". We had some conversation over what was going on, and there, we watched what happened at the opposite of the road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. So when you say then, when you were making these observations, it was not in fact at the front of the "White House" that you were making these observations, it was over the road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And so that was from what, around near the entrance area to the compound, the Potocari compound?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we were standing next to the road, 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: 50, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: 50 metres away?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: It's 30 metres to the road, so the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So a considerable distance, 30 to 50 metres observing this person?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And you would agree that there it was absolutely nothing distinctive about this person that you describe as not a plain soldier, was there? Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. My robe is caught on the chair unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Condon is glad to hear that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I'm glad, Your Honour. Very.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's really stuck.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I don't know whether to believe him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher. This is what we call a wardrobe malfunction, back home. Your Honour, the -- if I could just have the last question there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, her last question was [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. And so she said, would you agree that it was absolutely nothing distinctive about this person that you describe as not a plain soldier, was there? Well, and then I noticed you standing up or trying to stand up. And I think Ms. Condon interrupted her question there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's a twofold objection. The first is it's vague in terms of the term "nothing distinctive" and secondly, he has testified previously about this person that he observed and frankly certain memorable things about this individual that he retained in his memory. So it's been asked and answered to that extent as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you need to rephrase your question. You can rephrase it very easily apart from the description that you have already given us. Major Rutten, is there anything else that you could say about this individual that would be distinctive in -- as to his description?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Earlier I said the thing that was distinctive was that he was in command and not a plain soldier. That was what my -- arose my attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I'll rephrase my question, Your Honour, because what I'm putting to you, Major, is this: That insofar as the appearance, the physical appearance of this individual is concerned, you would agree that there was nothing distinctive about this person.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. And that stands to reason, does it not, because you simply gave, as we've already established, no description of this person in any of your statements.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So I want to ask you about your observation that you made in your proofing session on the 28th of November with Mr. Thayer, where you made this specific comment that this was a person who you considered to be in command and authority. That's what you said to Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And you would agree that you made absolutely -- in that regard at the proofing session with Mr. Thayer, you made no reference whatsoever to the fact of this person having given direct instructions to other Serb soldiers. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: That's -- that's difficult for me to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you this: What you said -- what -- I'll remind you of what you said on the 30th of November. This is at page 5, lines 12 to 13, Your Honour. You said that you had a specific recollection of this person giving direct instructions to other Serb soldiers. You accept that was your evidence --

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: -- in this trial? What I am putting to you is that you made, first of all, no reference in your evidence in Krstic, when you were asked about this, to this specific issue of giving direct instructions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And again, you made no reference in your proofing session to Mr. Thayer about this person giving direct instructions. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And we've already established, have we not, on Monday, that your memory ten years later could not be improved as to the details of what you recall about this day on the 13th of July 1995, could it?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No, it won't be improved. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And we've already established, have we not, that you can't speak B/C/S, Bosnian Serbo-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are continuing to repeat prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this objection. I'm leading somewhere in my cross-examination and I object to my learned friend's continual objections without foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's been successful in almost all of them except one.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think this question --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I'm leading somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This question was asked of him, so you don't need to remind the witness each time of each question that was put to him and how he has answered it. Go straight to the point, Ms. Condon.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: As to exactly what transpired between this person that you describe as not a plain soldier and the Serbian soldiers, you simply could not say, as to whether or not direct instructions were being given. You agree with that, you cannot say that?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Why? It's entirely a matter of presumption on your part, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No, it's not presumption. It's a professional overview, and you described me earlier as a professional, so I would give it back to you. I am a professional and I am seeing what I'm seeing and I'm observing quite well, I think, and I can make a distinction between a normal or plain soldier and someone who is in command. That's not only what I've learned but that's also the case through 25 years of experience, what I've seen and what I cannot see at a soldier and what he is doing. And I can see that from a certain distance because I've done that in several missions before.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well, if I just remind you of what you said in Krstic. This is at page 2152, lines 18 to 25, you're asked question: Now what did you observe him doing? This is the -- not a plain soldier. And your answer was: He was talking to the soldiers of the Bosnian Serb army. To me he looked like not a plain soldier because he spoke to everyone who was around. Do you agree that was your evidence?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So the words that you used there were that he was talking and he was speaking to people. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, speaking of your powers of observation, Major Rutten, I'd like you to have a look, please, at -- perhaps if we -- before we get rid of this photo, could you please initial this photo at the bottom and we'll save that.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Now, if P02103 could be brought up again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, which page?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: P01936 is the 65 ter number. That was the photo we just had up before. Sorry, got the -- perhaps we can use the ELMO again with this photo if there is some difficulty, Your Honour. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, just looking at this photo again. And I want you to focus -- perhaps it can be moved over to the left a little bit, Madam Usher. Thank you. I want to focus your attention on the gentleman on the right. Now, what you've said in relation to this photograph is, well, first of all, you say you can recognise this individual on the right, do you?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: From behind?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? Is that because you'd seen photos of this person many times before?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No. It's kind of a characteristic, if you look at the back of the head, you remember that, seeing that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You'd appreciate it's often very difficult to make an identification of somebody from behind. I'm not being facetious. You would appreciate it's difficult to identify somebody from behind?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes? So you say that it's not because you'd seen photos of this person before?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No? Not in the photo book that I -- that I showed you before, that's still in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking you, were there other photos of that individual in that photo book that you were shown by Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, from the first man also from the front side, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: M'hm, there were?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. And did you see those photos of the man on the right before you came to this photo in the photo book? Do you recall where they were in the sequence?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that in Krstic, this was a person who was in command on the 12th and 13th of July in and around Potocari, is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? Well, just let me ask you about the 12th of July. Tell me, where did you see him on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Do you mean the man on the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: The man on the right. I'm not interested in the man on the left any more. I'm focusing your mind on the gentleman on the right.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: On the road to Potocari. Sorry, on the road to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Talking with his men.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: With his men?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: How many times did you see him on the 12th of July, can you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And on the 13th of July, it's your evidence that this man on the right was also around the "White House"?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. Because what you've even said in this trial was that - this is at page 40, lines 10 and 11 today - is that the photo were the men that you probably saw at the "White House"?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Is that correct? So tell me, on what occasion did you see the man on the right at the "White House"? Was it on the first time you went there, was it on the second time, was it on the third time?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: It was during the time that we spent with the -- at the opposite of the road standing there with the Major De Haan and Rave where he had the discussion and at that moment I was seeing him there.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Again, I know I've asked you this already, but can you give me some specific time?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I already told you about the specific time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I appreciate it. It was in the afternoon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And you just simply cannot say whether or not it was 2, 3 or 4.00?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Tell me this, was at the time that you saw the man on the right, was that the same time frame that you saw the person that you described as not a plain soldier?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: In exact -- at the same time, but not in the same -- both in the vicinity of the "White House"?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No it was not at the same time. It was in the vicinity of the "White House", yes. They were not together.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Right. But it was in the same time frame?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was during the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Now, I've already asked you about your career advancement, Major. Can I just get some specifics as to what year you were promoted from Lieutenant to Captain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would appreciate hearing what the relevance of this line of questioning is going to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's the relevance of your question, Ms. Condon?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the context in which I cross-examined this witness as to his promotions and his commitment to his mission at Srebrenica, that is relevant to matters of his credit insofar as his willingness to cooperate with the many investigations that have been in relation to the fall of Srebrenica. In my submission, matters that go arguably to his credit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, respectfully, unless my learned colleague has a good faith basis on which to imply that this witness has any other motive to testify here other than the truth, then that line of questioning is frankly outrageous.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well, I object to that categorisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop. We'll stop this. But it's obviously hidden behind your desire to put the question is the idea you may have entertained in your mind already that the promotion is tied up with his willingness to cooperate with whichever authorities there may have been asking him or us -- asking him to come forward and answer questions. Which we will not allow. If you have got any evidence that that is so, then, yes, please let us know what the evidence is in his absence and we will decide to -- whether to authorise you to go ahead or not. But in the absence of concrete knowledge of such alleged or abuse, we will not let you do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: As Your Honour pleases. Just pardon me one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Major, when you testified in the Krstic trial, and we are talking about the transcript of the 5th of April, page 2104, 2105, you stated that one of your missions was to deliver humanitarian aid to the enclave. Could you please explain to us what was this humanitarian help that the DutchBat was supposed to deliver?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: The humanitarian aid consisted that we assisted also in repairing schools, the water supply, we assisted therein, for the enclave. We assisted on the UNHCR convoys that came in in the enclave, to the warehouse, and so on and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Talking about the UNHCR convoy, and you've stated on page 2105 in the Krstic trial, that there were a lot of formalities that had to be accomplished with the Serbs. What were these formalities that you had to do?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: There were no formalities that I had to do by myself. There were going through the battalion and it -- there were a lot of problems before an UNHCR convoy came through OP Papa and reached the enclave. I spoke to some drivers of that UNHCR convoys and they all told me that they had been quite a while on the road before entering the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you personally have not taken part in these formalities that were happening at the OP observation post, OP Papa observation post?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you talked about the drivers of the convoys, did you also talk about the situation that existed elsewhere, on other fronts in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: On some occasions, we spoke with them and they -- all drivers told us that there were problems of entering the enclaves because there was no freedom of movement whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge of a major Muslim offensive that took place in the spring of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I don't know what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Sarajevo front, amongst other fronts.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: That happened a lot, so you have to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I was talking to you about the Sarajevo surroundings, the offensive surrounding Sarajevo, the Muslim offensive around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: The only thing that we heard about it in the enclave were through the news channels. We got nothing, only a partly report about the surrounding of Sarajevo and that was it through the UN channels.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you have no knowledge of the security on the roads where the convoys were passing, which were caused by the combat operations that may have taken place there?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: That could have been, but the drivers of the UNHCR convoys were speaking specifically of entering the enclave because we were talking about our situation and that was the situation that caused a lot of time. I was well aware of the fact that there were also other check-points throughout Bosnia. Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in fact, these other check-points that existed in Bosnia, amongst these check-points, there were also check-points of the ABiH army, right?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, in the areas that they controlled. There were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You arrived in Srebrenica in the month of January 1995. Can you tell us how many UNHCR convoys arrived in the enclave in the month of January 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Again, only a rough estimate, but I think two probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in the month of February?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: It's also an estimate, two, one or two.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And do you know what was the situation in March?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: In March, it was by the end of March because we had then reports about the total minimised situation in the enclave, also within the battalion. So yeah, we spoke a lot about it and in the end of March I came -- I think it was the end of March, I'm not quite sure, came another convoy, another UNHCR convoy, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in the month of April, were there any convoys from the UNHCR?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: To my recollection, not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Are you absolutely certain that there were no UNHCR convoys -- are you certain that you're talking about those convoys and not the convoys that were supposed to come and bring supplies to the DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I refer to UNHCR convoys, and if I'm talking to logistics for the battalion, then I will address that as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Very well. So you're stating that there were no UNHCR convoys in the month of April?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I said to my -- I already answered that question, I think. To my recollection, not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And then in the month of May, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Are you again asking about the convoys?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, Major.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: It's also again an estimation, probably one, because there came in some late one and we were surprised that there still was coming in one or two but probably it was one because we -- there was always a group on a reaction stand-by, if there was a convoy coming in through OP Papa, we assisted that convoy to the warehouse in Srebrenica. So -- and to my recollection, only -- and that is what to my recollection is, once in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And do you recall that any convoys arrived in June?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No, to my recollection, not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So you have absolutely no recollection of the problems that UNHCR convoys encountered with the DutchBat who were searching the convoys?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: We never searched the convoys. We had a clear eye on the drivers, because -- and that was already happened before they entered the enclave, by the Serbs. They were searching the convoys as well before they came in. But we searched as well, and we kept an eye on them as they were unloading next to the warehouse because a lot of the drivers could bring something along that we didn't want to have in the enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, I need to leave the courtroom for a couple of minutes. Please continue. Judge Prost will take over. I'll be back in a moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The search that you carried out for the UNHCR convoys, you were doing that on behalf of the army of the ABiH; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure this is lawful under Rule 16 bis because Judge Kwon is not here either. I may need a moment to look at it but sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: We will just take a moment here, thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, did you have a comment on that particular point?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: On my learned colleague Mr. Josse's point or on the previous question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: No. On Mr. Josse's point.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Until I consulted myself on Rule 15, Your Honour, I think the Prosecution's position is we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I think the problem is solved. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If you have doubts about that, Mr. Josse, Madam Fauveau can repeat the question and it can be answered. Madam Fauveau, you haven't put the question as yet in any case, so, all right, Love's Labours Lost and we proceed with your next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Major, whether you carried out the UNHCR convoy searches, was it on behalf of the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I don't believe that's an accurate characterisation of his testimony. I think he testified that they search the driver but not the convoy itself. So I think that's an inaccurate phrasing of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are not 100 per cent on this but I think you are right. I stand to be corrected, however. Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will reiterate my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you were searching the drivers of the convoys, was it on behalf of the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No. It was under our own authority there because we wanted that they, as I stated before, that they bring nothing in the enclave that we wouldn't have there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you recall some -- of some problems in the month of June and that UNHCR representatives threatened to stop everything that were -- all the convoys precisely because the DutchBat was searching them?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: To my knowledge, that never was a point, and I also got through the battalion that there was never the point. So I don't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You've stated on the 29th of November, on page 4807 of the transcript, that you obtained the information that there were -- that the reserves were depleting in Srebrenica, where the humanitarian aid was stocked. Did you go and see yourself to see what was left in the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: There was -- we were patrolling during a social patrol in Srebrenica, and with my patrol commander, I was at the warehouse and there was almost nothing left in the warehouse at the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, you've stated on the 30th of November, page 4869 of the transcript, that you heard that there was a black market in Srebrenica. Did you or had you heard that the ABiH army was using goods that were warehoused in the warehouse of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: There was a black market. That was known to us. We knew also that there was a kind of trade going on but we never could figure out whether it came from the warehouse or not, or it were goods that people of Srebrenica got and they traded it on to other people in the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, do you know that the Medecins Sans Frontieres organisation was in the enclave when you were there?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And do you know that there were some problems between the municipal authorities of Srebrenica and the MSF?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the Krstic trial, on page 2174, you've stated that you knew that the ABiH army was supplied by the southern route. Is it right to say that this supply also included military equipment?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And the DutchBat had -- did the DutchBat have an observation post on the southern part of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: There were more observation posts on the command of the Bravo Company in the southern part of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And how was it possible that this military equipment was able to get into the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: It was a hidden operation by the ABiH, probably, and we noticed that it happened later on, because we saw the goods during night-time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: To your opinion, was the DutchBat sufficiently armed?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 3D44, please. Page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, do you see, under the heading "Operational Activities," you said [In English] "immediate superior, he considered that they were sufficiently armed." [Interpretation] Sir, is this your statement, is this what you've stated?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: This is a statement of the debriefing in Assen, as I see it here, and it was a rewritten what I also addressed last week, a rewritten statement by the ministry. There were discussions before we went to the enclave to have our APCs, and that discussion is also laid down in the NIOD report, that we had a large discussion on the armament of the APCs. We wanted to have the APCs with a 25-millimetre canyons on it. We only got the ones with us with .50 gun on it. So sufficient or not, or insufficient armed, it means that we had almost no -- no ammunition or checked ammunition left or there came only a few percentage in the enclave with the first battalion DutchBat 1, and afterwards, almost nothing came in. The things that came in were hidden in some convoys of DutchBat convoys, logistics convoys, I mean now, and that was a very small amount of small armament or devices to check our antitank missiles.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, are you telling us that the things you said in Assen is inexact, that everything that was written in this document is inexact during your Assen debriefing? Is this what you're telling us today?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Not -- I addressed it also last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. He's just stated he has addressed that and more or less asked us to disregard almost in its entirety or their entirety, his statements he made in Assen. But of course that has already been stated, but if you want to be specific as to identify the parts from that statement and ask him to be more specific, then you may of course go ahead. But try to keep it as brief as possible because more or less this has been dealt with already, even with regard to the ammunition. He stated that there was a difference between when they first arrived and later periods. So we try to avoid as much repetition as possible, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You've stated that there was a difference between what happened when you arrived and later. Now, regarding ammunition, where was it spent?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: It wasn't -- almost none of the ammunition was spent, because we weren't in the position to spend any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You still need to give us an explanation. If, as it seems to be the case, at a certain point in time, according to you, the amount of ammunition available left much to be desired, then there must have been a reason. It's being put to you that this reason is that this ammunition that you had available before had been made use of. Is that the case or is there any other explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is another explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So please can you give us the other explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A lot of the ammunition we couldn't use any more because it came in with DutchBat III and it wasn't usable any more because there was a lot of risks to it to use that ammunition. So we stashed it in our warehouse on the compound itself and we didn't use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Not at all, Mr. President. Just a clarification for the record, the transcript indicates that it came in with DutchBat III. I don't know if that was a misstatement or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he said DutchBat III. That's what I heard him say. If he wishes to correct that, then let him come forward and correct it. But that's what he said, for sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It came in -- I didn't say that. It came in with DutchBat 1. With DutchBat 1, the ammo came in and then later on there came almost no ammo in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, while you were in the enclave, did you ever hear that there was an offer given to the Serbs that they supply the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I think that maybe there is a mistake in the interpretation. I asked you if you were aware that an offer was made by the Serbs that they should be the ones supplying the enclave.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You've stated on the 4th of December, on page 4960 of the transcripts, that you were regularly seeing the military personnel of the army of the ABiH. You were seeing soldiers wearing -- carrying arms. Did you not have the obligation to disarm these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes. We had that obligation. We made several attempts on that. But every time they fled or they didn't wear the weapons, and they always, the weapons that they had, the small arms and also the light guns, were hidden.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you saw the Muslims who were armed, were they always wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: They were always wearing uniforms or partly uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But you were able to see soldiers of the ABiH wearing civilian clothes, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: On the occasions that I saw that, I already explained that last week.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you know that the main headquarters of the 28th Division was stationed in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, we were aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On the 4th of December, on page 4959 of the transcript, you've stated that the Muslims were using a house in Potocari which was serving as a sort of a headquarters that they were there. The house or the houses that they were using, that the Muslims were using, can we describe those houses as being regular houses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's been asked and he's answered this very question previously. And, in fact, he circled the house on an exhibit in connection with my learned friend Ms. Condon's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What do you have to answer to that, Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the house to which my honourable confrere is referring to is not the house I'm referring to. My colleague is talking about the house where the meetings took place, but I'm talking about the Main Staff or the headquarters of the Muslim armed forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- I think she is -- Madam Fauveau is right. Please proceed. You are 100 per cent right. The house that he was asked to indicate before was the one where the meetings took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Major, the houses that were used in Potocari and around Potocari by the Muslim forces, these houses, were they just regular houses?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: If -- yeah, if there were houses that they were using, then it were regular houses, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You've stated a few moments ago that you have experience, which I do not doubt, but would you say that the headquarters of a brigade or a division is a military target?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You've stated on the 29th of November, and you've confirmed it on the 30th of November, page 4820 of the transcript of the 30th of November, that the Serbs were bombing houses on the Budak hill. Before those shellings or bombings, were you able to go and see those houses? Were you ever in a position to do so?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: The days before the shelling, almost all houses were left because they were in the shooting range from Burici hill, so it was quite dangerous to have there, to have there your HQ of brigades or whatsoever because you're quite an easy target.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This was not my question. This is not what I'm suggesting either. I wanted to know if you had ever gone to those houses.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So you cannot confirm that these houses were not used to store weapons or ammunition for the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure but the houses were on constant surveillance of the post of the entrance of the compound. So they could see, literally see, what was happening on that hill. And that post on the entrance of the compound was constantly manned by personnel from DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in fact, the southern border of the enclave was also under the surveillance of the DutchBat that was there?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, but then you're speaking about a much larger area where the lines of sight are -- were through the hilly terrain, were quite narrow or quite bordered. So you couldn't identify what was happening until five, 4 or 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On the base of Potocari, where these houses were situated, was there any power, electricity?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: The only electricity that we had was through generators of DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Therefore, during night, it was quite dark, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you recognise that you couldn't see exactly what was going on during night in those houses?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: We had also a platoon of 108 Commando Company aboard, and a lot of soldiers from 108 were outside of the compound during night-time, so we had quite a real estimate of what was going on during night-time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But the military of the DutchBat, which were in the southern part of the enclave, had also patrols, no?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they had also patrols, but always the patrols were during day-time because there was also a UN rules of engagements and protocol that the posts on the -- the observations post should be lighted throughout the night with the blue flag marked on the observation post. So you could quite good -- quite see us, but if you have to look from out the light into the darkness, it's quite difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that your Lieutenant Colonel Karremans, on the 10th July, had about 1700 men armed in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: This is totally new to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This may be a transcript issue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I didn't notice you because I was looking at it and I was saying this I could understand more than one way, because as it is in the transcript, it seems to hint that the DutchBat itself --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I suggest that you repeat your question and we'll get fresh interpretation. Because I was looking at it and I was saying, does she know what she is asking? Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that your commander, Lieutenant Colonel Karremans, saw, in the evening of the 10th of July, about 1500 armed men in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: This is a question you have to raise to Lieutenant Colonel Karremans and not to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'm not asking if he had seen it. I'm asking you if you have knowledge, if you're aware of that. Did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said in the Krstic case, on the 11th of July 1995, the Serbs shelled the column which was going from Srebrenica to Potocari. Is it true that on the 11th of July 1995 you were in the bases of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And, personally, you haven't seen the shelling of the column?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: That is correct. But last week I also explained that I had two sets of radio with me and now I'm explaining it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is not my question. My question is, did you see?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said in the Krstic case, page 2111, that on the Tuesday morning, it would have been 11 July 1995, you were in the shelter because of the shelling. Is it not true that you were indeed inside the shelter because you heard the air attacks against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I also explained last week that I spent almost no time in the shelter. I was always outside, being with the group of men, or somewhere else around on the compound or outside of the compound. So shelter, we had no shelter, the shelter that we had was just the factory itself, inside the factory, and that was our shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Isn't it true that on the Tuesday morning, I'm talking about the members of the DutchBat and not you personally, you received an order to go into the shelter? Isn't it true?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Isn't it true that indeed this order was given because the air attacks on the position -- Serb positions were expected?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the Krstic case, page 2108, you said that the Serbs -- I'm talking about July, on the attack, 1995, you said that the Serbs were trying to confine you in your bases, so -- in your compound, so that you couldn't go out. Are you aware of the fact that the DutchBat was supposed to help the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in case of an attack on the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: We had no such orders whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown P2263. Could this document be shown in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is an order sent by the -- to Captain Groen by Major Franken. A simple question first. Have you seen this order before today?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you know this order was -- had been given?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No. Because this was an order given out to the B Company. It was a separated order. And if there was a separate order to the other company, my company commander was there, the one that had the knowledge of that, but I didn't have the knowledge of this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Are you -- do you agree that on this order you can see --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for sake of clarification, I'm not a B/C/S reader, but I'm looking at the document that's posted on the right in B/C/S and I'm just not sure whether it's the same document that's appearing in English, and I don't know if my learned colleagues who can read B/C/S can help us out. I just want to make sure there is no confusion for anybody here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Even at the --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is definitely not the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But previously we had two pages, both in B/C/S, and that's when Madam Fauveau said, "Could we see the English version?" So from then onwards, I was following the English version of course because I can't read B/C/S. So what's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't want the accused to be deprived from -- of the possibility of looking at this document. So could we upload this document also in B/C/S and we've seen it any way, and I suppose that Madam Fauveau is interested in the section, this seriously intended green assignment. But can we have it in B/C/S as well, please. What we have on the right is a translation of this document, but it's certainly not the same page. But can we go to the first page of this document. Of the B/C/S, yeah. But it's certainly not the same one. I have no doubt in my mind. I mean, I don't understand the language or -- I understand very little of it, but it's -- even -- you don't even need to understand the language to realise that it's not the same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I continue? May I suggest we continue, because the objection was made by the Prosecutor. It's not my fault if they didn't show the proper document in B/C/S in the system. For the moment, we only need the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Major, can you see on this document the sentence, "This is a serious intended green assignment"?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when such a sentence appears on an order of the United Nations forces, could you explain what this means?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: It means that we, as a UN unit, we go into combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And this means in general, at least in such a situation here, because if you look at paragraph which is just before, that you're taking part for one part in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No. We are not taking part in the conflict. There is a serious threat coming from the south side, from the Serb side, and we have to engage that threat and staying impartial and not taking up for the Bosnia-Herzegovina army, for the ABiH. But for safety reasons, we have to go into a green role, as we say that, but we go into a green role with blue helmets and white APCs, so there is a slight problem there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I will reformulate or rephrase my question. You don't take parties for a party in the conflict, but you certainly take a party against one of the parties to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, because one of the parties is taken up an aggressive act to the area that we have to -- to have to safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you know about a meeting which took place in the night between 10 and 11 July 1995 between the representatives of civil powers and military Muslims and representatives of the DutchBat, in particular, Boering and Colonel Karremans?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that action was discussed, a joint action, of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the DutchBat was discussed during this meeting? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Not at that period of time. Later on, I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that before July 1995, to be precise, in May 1995, the representatives of military and civil powers in Srebrenica had had a meeting with Major Franken and that meeting was about the defence of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: During the morning meetings with the battalion, we heard there were several meetings with the Bosnian army where they tried to -- to, yes, more or less convince us to take part in the defence of the army on the side of the ABiH, but we never did so.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina came out of the enclave and attacked the villages, southern villages around, you never defended those villages, did you?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: We weren't aware of the fact what was happening outside of the borders of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But being inside, you never tried to prevent the military of -- the military of Bosnia-Herzegovina to go out of the enclave. You never tried to prevent them to go out of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: They didn't tell us aforehand what they going to plan to and it was known to us whether they did so. So we also could nothing prevent.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But you knew that the military equipment which came into the enclave, that you didn't prevent it either?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I already addressed that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, I think you were going to object.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said on 30 November, page 4884 of the note, that members of DutchBat were assisting the population of Srebrenica to go to Potocari. This is on the 11th of July. Is it true that the trucks and the APCs belonging to the DutchBat were being used to transport the population?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What was the means of transportation of the population in Srebrenica to Potocari on the 11th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: On the 11th, as I recall it, the first came in but not with our APCs. And only at the late evening or afternoon, some -- afternoon, yes, I think, some trucks from the B Company brought and also from the battalion itself, brought in some refugees from Srebrenica, but not using any APCs for carrying Muslim people to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that some of these APCs actually ran over some people? Or made them fall?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that fact. There were a lot of rumours those days and I'm don't know at this point whether that was rumours or did happen, because most of the APCs of the B Company stayed and also of the battalion, stayed at the south side on the 11th. Only later on they moved on towards the northern part, so towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 3D50, with a Dutch version 3D49.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- documents at the same time in the system, so it will be one and then after, the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suggest what we can do, we can have one on the system and one on the ELMO and we try to work out that way. If that is helpful. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I could see the Dutch version, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we have the Dutch version in the system? This is the -- this is the other document that we had before. What I see on the screen now is what allegedly was page 1 of that -- so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could page 23 of the English version be shown? And Major, to help you, it is page 11 of the Dutch version.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the last paragraph of that page 23 in English, you can read, [French translation coming over English channel] ... "armoured personnel carrier ran over some people and that there were a set of circumstances. I said then I think the application of criminal sanction in order to find these people but do something about it." [Interpretation] Major, I'm not at all interested in a question of liability. What I'm interested in is simply the fact: Do you know as a fact that the APCs would have run over certain people?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: The situation that I have in front of me is something different from what you're asking, because you're asking me about the 11th of July, of the people that are fleeing from Srebrenica towards Potocari, and what we here read is the situation that what I'm talking about, and that's not exactly in this piece of paper, but that's the situation that the group of personnel from DutchBat, from OP Mike or OP November had to fall back because of the shelling. There were some problems with the ABiH because they hated it that DutchBat left those OPs. At a certain stage, the OP commander said to his personnel to get into the APC and he then had to move because of the shelling towards -- from November towards Potocari. And there is a very narrow road in the mountainous area, and there probably have been people ran over and that was part of an investigation later on on the Dutch side. And that's the reason why I mentioned it here because one of the medical personnel was one of -- one of the soldiers out of my platoon and he told me later on. So I addressed that to my company commander and later on, in the management report, as we heard it before, and that's the reason why I told it here in the van Kemenade report.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for these clarifications. Could you tell us the date of this incident?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: This is all OPs, almost at the northern part, were left at the -- at the 11th, late in the evening, 11th or at night towards the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that the great majority of people coming to Potocari were women and children?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Mostly women and children, boys and older men, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could it be said that most of the able-bodied men did not go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it is in a most direct manner implied in his answer. You don't need to answer -- ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that since women and children, boys and elder people came to Potocari while able-bodied men did not go to Potocari, could it be said that indeed there was a separation between the males and females, the non-military who went to Potocari and the military population who did not go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had extensive question and answering on this very issue with my learned colleague Mr. Lazarevic's cross-examination of Major Rutten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you agree to that, Ms. Fauveau? Because I think that was more or less covered even along the same line of questioning that -- and formulation that you have just adopted.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's just one question I want and then I'll pass to another subject immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's hear what the question is but please don't try to repeat a question that someone else, one of your colleagues, has put.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Would you agree that indeed there was a separation between the female population and non-military population arrived in Potocari while the military population did not come to Potocari? That's the question I've just asked. It's the same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He answered that. He has answered that already, when he was being questioned by -- Mr. Thayer suggested it was Mr. Lazarevic, but to be honest with you, I don't remember who it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Mr. Thayer thinks it was so clear, could he then perhaps tell me what is the page or transcript or line of note where it appears?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, Ms. Fauveau. If you are not happy with the -- we are assuring you that that question was put. We are assuring you that that question was answered. If you want to pursue the matter, insofar as you think that the witness's answer was not complete and that you would like to elicit more information from him, you can put to him his previous answer, then put your next question and we'll proceed accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure that the witness never answered this question but I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Answering this question --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we agree with the Prosecution that the witness answered yes to that question? Can we agree with this, Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will stand corrected on one issue, that is, the questions came from my learned colleague, I believe Mr. Josse. And this question was asked and answered. That's as far as I'm going to agree to anything. Let's, please, move on. This is wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was Mr. Lazarevic, now it's Mr. Josse. I'm sure there was no answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was more precise in telling you I couldn't remember who it was, but I do remember the question being asked, maybe not in exactly the same formulation as yours, and answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you that it was asked indeed, but I'm not in agreement with the rest. And the answer. But I will continue, of course, if you order me to continue or to go to another subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your choice, Madam Fauveau, but if you want to pursue this matter, it's only insofar as you refer him directly to his previous answer and if you're not happy with it, you want to get more information or some clarification from the witness, you can certainly do that, but otherwise, move to your next area of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that it is time to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And for you to find the transcript, now that we know, or at least we think we know that it was Mr. Josse that put the question. I mean, Mr. Josse's cross-examination wasn't a long one and we can go there. We'll have a -- how much more time do you have, do you require, Ms. Fauveau? Madam Fauveau? How much more time do you require?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 15 minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We are safe. And you're still in the region of a few minutes, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm tempted to say that really depends on how much Mr. Thayer interrupts me, but, yes, ten to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer is already interrupting. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm not making an objection. I was just standing because I see Madam Usher, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So we'll have a 30-minute break starting from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, on the 30th of November, 2006, page 4835, my colleague asked you if, regarding Potocari, there was a natural separation made between women and children, and you've indicated that on the map. My question is slightly different. What I'm asking you is to find out the following: Was there a separation between able-bodied men and the non-military population that was not in Potocari but that was there before the non-military population arrived in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the specific question to which my learned colleague is referring was specific as to natural separation taking place between men and women. That question was answered. A different version of the question was then asked later on in which Major Rutten described Muslim men departing the area to the area of Buljim which he in fact marked on an exhibit. This question has been asked and answered with great specificity both in the question and in the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I quite agree with you, Mr. Thayer. Let's move to the next question, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, are you saying that only the non-military population came to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think I can anticipate your objection. He's already answered that. He's said on a previous occasion but --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There were some and they left towards the mountain or the hills or whatever they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Since only the non-military population came to Potocari, do you know where the non-military population went?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Twofold objection, Mr. President. The first is that wasn't his testimony and secondly, he's already answered to the best of his ability, given the previous questions, the second part of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I couldn't agree more. I think I suggest you move to something different, because you keep hammering this in different forms and from different angles and it boils down to the same thing, that you are asking the witness to repeat what he has already explained to us. And one draws the obvious conclusions from what he has stated earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will go to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it exact to say that you left approximately 5.000 people in the Potocari compound belonging to the UN in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it exact to say that you left 5.000 people?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: First, you asked me the question approximately and now you're asking me exact. I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Maybe there is an interpretation error. My question is the following: Is it exact to say that you could have left more than 5.000 people in the Potocari compound?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: The reason that -- I put it like this: We could shelter 5.000, approximately 5.000, into the old factory. We could have let in more people on the compound but then they were in the open air and we saw that as a risk.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And where they were outside, they were not under -- they were not in open air?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes, but they were under surveillance of the DutchBat troops there. And not only that, but from the hills of Purici, you couldn't exactly see the total environment of the bus compound, but you could see the total environment of the compound from DutchBat in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Talking about the bodies that you've discovered, the nine bodies that you discovered, you said this on the 30th of November on page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: -- that you examined the bodies. Could you describe to us what were the injuries that you were able to notice?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I already explained that in an earlier statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, can you or, rather, were these people dressed, those bodies that you discovered? Were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: I also explained that earlier. They were dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when you examined the bodies, did you take off their clothes? Did you undress the bodies that you found?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: How can you then tell us that you were able to see the injuries?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: We saw the holes of small arms weapons in the bodies because they were shot through the clothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were you able to see the holes in the clothes or were you also able to see the injuries on the bodies themselves?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: We could see the holes in the clothes, the blood and the -- and partly the injuries in the -- on the bodies itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So the injuries, you've seen them only partially, if I'm not mistaken. What was the size of the injuries that you were able to observe, if you were able to measure the size of the wounds?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: As I said before, it were shot wounds from small calibre weapons, in-shot wounds and they are very clearly what they call and what they inflict on the human bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This was not my question. I just wanted to know what was the size of the wounds or the injuries and not with what those injuries were caused.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: The size was an in-shot hole, what you see on a body if you were having a shot wound on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By in-shot, we mean entry wound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, yes, an entry wound. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to know what was the size. Could you please talk to me in centimetres or can you use also another type of measure if you wish, but tell us how wide or how big were those injuries?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: The size of a pinky.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We just need some clarification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A small, a very small -- the size of a finger, a small finger, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it exact to say that you do not know if those bodies belonged to men who, before they were killed, were the same men who were in the Potocari base?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think, if I remember well, but I think I do remember, that he was asked the question whether he recognised those men and he said no, never seen them before. So I suppose he can't answer your question. Do I remember well, Major?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you're right on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you do not know if these men were members of the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: No, because they were unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Talking about the refugees that were in Potocari, is it exact to say that the population in Potocari, that came to Potocari on the 11th of July, was not able to stay in Potocari for a very long time?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And can we say that those people, at any rate, did not wish to stay in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES HENDRIKUS ANTONIUS RUTTEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, this is my last question. Could the witness be shown evidence 3D50. It is the exhibit that we cannot see at the same time in Dutch and in English. In English, we are talking about page 8 and in Dutch it's page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's adopt the same procedure as before. The Dutch version will be placed on the ELMO and on the screen we'll have the English translation thereof.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
